title: Operating Systems Fundamentals

steps.title: What an operating system does
steps.content: An operating system manages hardware and provides services for programs. Core responsibilities include process management, memory management, files, devices, security and scheduling.
steps.example: When you open a browser, the OS creates or schedules processes and manages memory and device access.

steps.title: Process versus program
options: A program stored on disk only
steps.explanation: A process is an executing instance of a program with its own execution state and resources.

steps.title: Process scheduling
steps.content: The scheduler decides which ready process receives CPU time. Context switching saves one process's state and loads another's. Switching has overhead, so it is not free.
steps.tip: A process is a running program; a thread is an execution path within a process.

steps.title: Understand deadlock
steps.prompt: Which condition is one of the classic necessary conditions for deadlock?
steps.explanation: The four Coffman conditions include mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait.

steps.title: Virtual memory
steps.content: Virtual memory gives each process a virtual address space. The OS and hardware translate virtual addresses to physical memory; pages may be loaded on demand.
steps.example: A page fault occurs when a referenced page is not currently mapped in physical memory and must be resolved.

questions.prompt: Which is a core operating-system responsibility?
questions.explanation: The OS manages memory resources for processes.
A process is an executing program instance.

options: Saving and restoring execution state between processes/threads
questions.explanation: The CPU switches execution by saving one state and restoring another.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the four classic deadlock conditions?
questions.explanation: The four conditions are mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait.

options: A request for a page not currently present in physical memory
questions.explanation: The memory system must resolve a reference to a page that is not currently resident.

learning_objectives: Describe CPU scheduling and context switching.
Understand memory management and virtual memory.
Connect operating-system concepts to everyday behavior.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A process and a thread are identical.
common_misconceptions.correction: A process has its own address space; threads within it share process resources.

common_misconceptions.misconception: More threads always make a program faster.
common_misconceptions.correction: Synchronization and scheduling overhead can reduce performance.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Deadlock means a process is merely slow.
common_misconceptions.correction: Deadlock is a circular wait in which involved processes cannot make progress.

worked_examples.title: Process versus thread
worked_examples.input: A browser runs tabs and background tasks.
trace: A process can contain multiple threads.
Threads in one process share its memory space.
worked_examples.output: A process is a resource boundary; a thread is an execution path
worked_examples.explanation: This distinction helps explain isolation, communication and concurrency.

worked_examples.title: Context switching
worked_examples.input: CPU switches from process A to process B
trace: Resume B at its saved instruction.
worked_examples.output: The CPU continues with process B
worked_examples.explanation: Context switching enables multitasking but has overhead.

worked_examples.title: Recognize deadlock
worked_examples.input: P1 holds R1 and waits for R2; P2 holds R2 and waits for R1.
trace: Each waits for a resource held by the other.
worked_examples.output: Deadlock cycle: P1 → R2 → P2 → R1 → P1
worked_examples.explanation: A circular wait can prevent both processes from progressing.

company_applications.practice: Explain processes, threads, scheduling and deadlocks.
Use small examples to explain synchronization and memory.
Compare concepts clearly and identify trade-offs.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Operating Systems Fundamentals?
srs_cards.answer: Explain process and thread differences. Describe CPU scheduling and context switching. Understand memory management and virtual memory. Explain synchronization and deadlocks. Connect operating-system concepts to everyday behavior.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Operating Systems Fundamentals.
srs_cards.answer: A process has its own address space; threads within it share process resources.
